::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[I want to solve the equation](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1149126/i-want-to-solve-the-equation), asked by [VihangaAW](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/195616/vihangaaw) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-02-15; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> How to show the equation $4 \sin(x) +3 \cos (x)$ as $r \sin (x-\alpha)$
>
> I tried to solve this using $a \cos(x)+b \sin(x) = c$. But there aren't any to use as $c$
:::

The angle-addition formula
$$\sin(x-\alpha) = \sin(x)\cos(\alpha) - \cos(x)\sin(\alpha)$$
will help you set up a system of equations for $r$ and $\alpha$.
